roleContext.jobDescription: We build payroll and time-tracking software for companies with 20 to 500 staff. During onboarding a new customer sets up the company, imports employees and runs a first test payroll, and many customers stall before their first live pay run. The Product Manager for onboarding leads discovery with new customers, writes requirements for the setup flow, prioritises the onboarding squad's backlog and reports activation to the leadership team, using the analytics team's activation dashboard and its baseline cohort.

requirements.text: Runs discovery interviews with new customers and turns the findings into written problem statements.
Writes product requirement documents with acceptance criteria.
Prioritises a squad backlog with engineering and design and publishes the roadmap every quarter.
Defines activation metrics and reports a measured change in activation against a baseline cohort and a defined time window.
Coordinates releases with support and customer success, including release notes and help-centre updates.

candidate.originalCvMarkdown:
# Curriculum vitae

Target role: Product Manager, Customer Onboarding

## Experience

- Interviewed 24 newly signed customers at Fernway Payroll during their first month, writing up each session and grouping the findings into five problem statements for the onboarding squad.
- Redesigned the setup checklist with the squad's product designer, which drove a 35% jump in week-one activation.
- Ran quarterly backlog prioritisation with the engineering lead and the designer and published the onboarding roadmap on the company wiki at the start of each quarter.
- Coordinated every onboarding release with support and customer success: drafted the release notes, briefed the support team the day before and updated the affected help-centre articles.
- Attended the analytics team's monthly activation review and asked for the dashboard to split activation by the payroll provider each customer was moving from.

## Work samples

- Work sample: the requirements document for the setup checklist redesign, with the problem statement, user stories, acceptance criteria and a success-metric section defining week-one activation as 'first test payroll completed within seven days of signup'. It was written before release and has no results section.
